W1.title: S6 embedder timing on both classes
W1.note: Image built with EMBEDDER_VARIANT=fp32 and KEEP_UNPATCHED=1 (both models, /srv/models/embedder_timing.py and /srv/models/embed_rss.py); 60 interleaved rounds plus the salt-format set; the shared class twice (fresh, burst-drained). Decides the embedder on memory as well as speed: embed_rss measures the resident memory the timing script cannot (it holds both models in one process). RISK, UNVERIFIED: the first fp32 Docker build runs the in-build gates (bit-exact dequantization, then the cosine gate with the 8-bit session and the 2.3 GB fp32 session alive: about 3 GB of models in memory) on Fly's remote builder, whose memory for this org is not known; if the build is killed it needs a larger builder or a local build (scripts/staging.py deploy always passes --remote-only, so a local build is by hand). Remote-builder minutes are unpriced.
steps: scripts/staging.py quote W1, then create W1 --org <org> --approve-quote 0.08 (owner approval first).

Deploy to the first class: scripts/staging.py deploy W1 api --class shared-cpu-2x:4gb --build-arg EMBEDDER_VARIANT=fp32 --build-arg KEEP_UNPATCHED=1. The image holds both models, /srv/models/embedder_timing.py and /srv/models/embed_rss.py. For the second class run it again with --class performance-2x:4gb (a second build unless the builder's cache holds it).

UNVERIFIED: W1 has no database, so the serve process of that machine cannot become healthy. Do not measure next to it (it shares the 4 GB and the cores with the probe): stop it, or run each command below on a one-off machine of the same image and class (flyctl machine run), and destroy that machine after. Decide this before the window.

On each class, first (the shared class still holds its burst balance): python /srv/models/embedder_timing.py /srv/models/qwen3-embedding-0.6b-q8/model_q8.onnx /srv/models/qwen3-embedding-0.6b-fp32/model_fp32.onnx -n 60 --threads 1 --out /tmp/timing.json, then cat /tmp/timing.json (--out - writes a file named '-', it does not print). Repeat on the shared class once the balance is drained.

On performance-2x:4gb, in two separate processes, q8 first: python /srv/models/embed_rss.py /srv/models/qwen3-embedding-0.6b-q8/model_q8.onnx --out /tmp/rss_q8.json, then python /srv/models/embed_rss.py /srv/models/qwen3-embedding-0.6b-fp32/model_fp32.onnx --compare /tmp/rss_q8.json --out /tmp/rss_fp32.json. Each prints one JSON object. Memory does not depend on the CPU class and each run is about 4 minutes of full-core work, which would drain a shared core's burst balance: on shared-cpu-2x:4gb run them only after its timing, last, and do not read their times as gate evidence.

Read the fp32 JSON: gate_evidence must be true; verdict PASS or FAIL against 2,400,000 kB with margin_kb; rss_anon_kb and rss_file_kb at after_passages say whether the 2.3 GB data file is resident or private memory.

Record by hand (no script writes artifacts/m5_spikes.json; its owner merges): both timing JSONs under S6_fly_timing (one per class and run) and both embed_rss JSONs under S6_fly_rss. Neither JSON holds a secret or a path.
scripts/staging.py destroy W1 --yes.

W1b.title: fp32 embedder memory confirmation: the real uvicorn, 3 fresh boots
W1b.duration: 3 fresh boots of about 10 min each (create to healthy, then one max-size upload with mock-LLM asks at the live caps)
W1b.note: Council 7, decision 1, step 3 (docs/v2/research/m5-councils/council7/verdict.md). The REAL service (python -m semigraph.serve.drain) on a fresh shared-cpu-2x / 4 GB machine in sin with the fp32 embedder image that would ship (EMBEDDER_VARIANT=fp32, NO KEEP_UNPATCHED: scripts/staging.py refuses the other combinations for this window), the staging database and the mock LLM. The api app uses deploy/staging/fly.w1b.toml: the staging environment with the live memory settings (fp32 model path, EMBED_SLOTS=1, MAX_CONCURRENT_ANSWERS=2, the code-default upload caps, swap_size_mb=1024). Load per boot (tools/probe/w1b.py): M4's max-size upload (tests/upload_fixtures.max_size_pdf(30, 2700)) plus salted mock-LLM asks, at most the live in-flight cap concurrently, from the upload's acceptance until the job is ready plus 30 s. PASS (pre-registered, do not change), on EVERY boot: max VmHWM of the uvicorn process <= 2,400,000 kB (inclusive), no OOM kill and no process restart, machine creation to /healthz 200 <= 180 s (inclusive). Reported besides: the spread of the three peaks, the lowest MemAvailable, the swap used. Memory, not latency, is measured, so the mock runs on the cheap class. The remote build of the api image is not priced here (builder minutes are not in the rates).
steps: scripts/staging.py quote W1b, then create W1b --org <org> --approve-quote 0.10 (owner approval first), then seed W1b and deploy W1b mockllm.

scripts/staging.py deploy W1b api --build-arg EMBEDDER_VARIANT=fp32 (the tool refuses a missing EMBEDDER_VARIANT=fp32 and any KEEP_UNPATCHED=1 here), then preflight W1b. This first machine is a warm-up that proves the build and the deployed configuration: it is not a measured boot.

For each measured boot n = 1, 2, 3: flyctl machine list -a semigraph-stg --json, flyctl machine destroy <id> --force -a semigraph-stg for every machine that is not destroyed, then START the driver BEFORE the deploy (as a background job or in a second terminal): python -m tools.probe.w1b boot --boot n --wait-for-machine-s 2700 --out <dir>/boot-n.json, then scripts/staging.py deploy W1b api --build-arg EMBEDDER_VARIANT=fp32 (a fresh machine id and creation time), then wait for the driver. Started first, the driver polls /healthz from the new machine's creation; started after the deploy it would find the machine already healthy and could not time the boot (such a boot is INCONCLUSIVE when over 180 s).
python -m tools.probe.w1b aggregate <dir>/boot-1.json <dir>/boot-2.json <dir>/boot-3.json --out <dir>/w1b.json: PASS only if all three boots pass.
Record by hand (no script writes artifacts/m5_spikes.json; its owner merges): the aggregate under S6_w1b. It holds no secret.
scripts/staging.py snapshot W1b --out <dir>, then scripts/staging.py destroy W1b --yes.

W1c.title: fp32 embedder memory confirmation, paced ask load: the real uvicorn, 3 fresh boots
W1c.duration: 3 fresh boots of about 10 to 25 min each (create to healthy, then one max-size upload with up to 14 paced mock-LLM asks, one per 30 s), plus at most one unchanged re-run of each INVALID boot

workload.derivation: floor(production max_spend_usd_per_day / the live hybrid estimate) = floor(10 / 0.709573) = floor(14.09) = 14

W1c.note: Council 8, 'The Recommendation' 2, W1c (docs/v2/research/m5-councils/council8/verdict.md). W1c is window W1b with ONE change, the ask workload: the same apps (api, neo4j, mockllm), the same api toml (deploy/staging/fly.w1b.toml), the same build-argument policy (EMBEDDER_VARIANT=fp32 required, KEEP_UNPATCHED=1 refused), the same machines, classes and hours, 3 FRESH boots, the same PASS thresholds and the same INVALID rule. Reason: W1b's saturating ask load (~150 asks) starved the upload past its 1,200 s embed timeout on the throttled machine (boot 2 INVALID twice, memory within limits each time); council 8 chose a paced load anchored to the live day cap; the memory thresholds are unchanged. Workload per boot (tools/probe/w1b.py --window W1c, tools/probe/paced_asks.py): at most 14 salted mock-LLM asks (the cap). 14 = floor(production max_spend_usd_per_day / the live hybrid estimate) = floor(10 / 0.709573) = floor(14.09) = 14, computed in code from semigraph.config.PRODUCTION_MAX_SPEND_USD_PER_DAY and semigraph.serve.estimate for the fly.toml models (the driver refuses to run when the workload.asks registered here is not the count it derives). Pacing: one ask every 30 s from upload accept (the first ask at upload accept, so 14 asks span 390 s), each ask from a different X-Test-Client-IP, at most 2 in flight (when two are still in flight at the moment the next is due, the next waits and the delay is recorded, not skipped); sending stops at job ready plus 30 s, so the 14 is a cap and not a target (the boot records how many went out); measurement runs until the upload job is ready plus 30 s. The boot JSON records the window, the workload mode, the schedule (planned against actual send times) and the derivation. PASS (pre-registered, unchanged from W1b), on EVERY boot: max VmHWM of the uvicorn process <= 2,400,000 kB (inclusive), no OOM kill and no process restart, machine creation to /healthz 200 <= 180 s (inclusive); the aggregate passes only for exactly three boots on three different machines that all pass. INVALID (unchanged): the upload job did not reach ready, or no ask finished while it ran. Stop rule: an INVALID boot is re-run unchanged ONCE; if still INVALID, W1c is INCOMPLETE and nothing else is amended; a memory FAIL is a FAIL. (An INCONCLUSIVE boot is not re-run by this rule.) W1b's apps must be destroyed first: the app names are shared. The remote build of the api image is not priced here (builder minutes are not in the rates).
steps: scripts/staging.py quote W1c, then create W1c --org <org> --approve-quote 0.10 (owner approval first; W1b's window must be destroyed before: scripts/staging.py destroy W1b --yes, the app names are shared), then seed W1c and deploy W1c mockllm.

scripts/staging.py deploy W1c api --build-arg EMBEDDER_VARIANT=fp32 (the tool refuses a missing EMBEDDER_VARIANT=fp32 and any KEEP_UNPATCHED=1 here), then preflight W1c. This first machine is a warm-up that proves the build and the deployed configuration: it is not a measured boot.

For each measured boot n = 1, 2, 3: flyctl machine list -a semigraph-stg --json, flyctl machine destroy <id> --force -a semigraph-stg for every machine that is not destroyed, then START the driver BEFORE the deploy (as a background job or in a second terminal): python -m tools.probe.w1b boot --window W1c --boot n --wait-for-machine-s 2700 --out <dir>/boot-n.json, then scripts/staging.py deploy W1c api --build-arg EMBEDDER_VARIANT=fp32 (a fresh machine id and creation time), then wait for the driver. The driver reads the window's secrets from the W1c state file and the workload from this entry; it refuses a --tail-s or --concurrency that differs from it.

Only a boot whose JSON verdict is INVALID, and only if it has no attempt-2 file yet, is re-run ONCE, unchanged: the same commands with the same --boot n and --attempt 2 (python -m tools.probe.w1b boot --window W1c --boot n --attempt 2 --wait-for-machine-s 2700 --out <dir>/boot-n-a2.json), on a freshly created machine again (the README loop reads each boot-n.json and decides by its verdict). Keep the attempt-1 file. No other boot is re-run, and an INCONCLUSIVE one is not re-run by this rule.

python -m tools.probe.w1b aggregate with EVERY boot file of <dir> (boot-*.json: the three attempt-1 files and every boot-n-a2.json, so no attempt can be left out) --out <dir>/w1c.json: PASS only if the three deciding boots pass; INCOMPLETE if a boot is INVALID twice (stop, amend nothing) or still has no re-run (rerun_due); FAIL if any attempt fails.
Record by hand (no script writes artifacts/m5_spikes.json; its owner merges): the aggregate under S6_w1c, with W1b's INCOMPLETE record and its four boots kept as stress data. It holds no secret.
scripts/staging.py snapshot W1c --out <dir>, then scripts/staging.py destroy W1c --yes.
